q: What does the annual reconciliation compare?
options: The audited books (turnover, tax and ITC) with GSTR-9, which summarises the year's GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and GSTR-2B
exp: For larger taxpayers, GSTR-9C sets out this reconciliation formally.

q: Why must turnover be reconciled GSTIN by GSTIN, not just for the whole company?
options: Books are kept per company (PAN) but GST returns are per GSTIN, and supplies between the company's own GSTINs count as turnover for GST
exp: Inter-branch supplies disappear in consolidated books but are real supplies for GST.

q: Which GSTR-9 table shows the gap between ITC in GSTR-2B and ITC claimed?
exp: 8A is auto-populated from 2B, and 8D is the difference that officers often ask about.

q: At year end, a services client's books show ₹20 lakh of unbilled revenue (work done in March, invoiced in April within 30 days) and ₹10 lakh of advances received in March for work starting in April. Which needs GST for March?
options: The ₹10 lakh advance, since GST on advances for services is due when received; the unbilled revenue is a timing item
exp: Advances for goods don't attract GST, but advances for services do.

q: Which statement is filed with GSTR-9 by larger taxpayers to set out the books-vs-returns reconciliation?
options: GSTR-9C, self-certified, for aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore
exp: Since FY 2020-21 it no longer needs a CA's certificate.

q: Extra tax found in the annual reconciliation is paid through DRC-03, not through GSTR-9 itself.
exp: GSTR-9 records the year; payments of additional tax go through DRC-03 with interest.

q: Why should the annual reconciliation start well before the GSTR-9 due date of 31 December?
options: Because 30 November is the last date to claim missed ITC, amend GSTR-1 and issue credit notes for the year; after that, gaps can only be paid, not fixed
Because GSTR-9 opens only in October
Because auditors need it by September
exp: Reconciling in September to November keeps options open.

q: A client asks what the annual reconciliation involves and why you want to start in September. Explain.
model: It compares the audited books with what was reported for the year, GSTIN by GSTIN: turnover (taxable, exempt, exports, branch transfers), tax paid, and ITC against GSTR-2B. Starting early matters because 30 November is the last date to claim any missed ITC for the year, to amend GSTR-1 entries and to issue credit notes that reduce tax. After that, extra tax can only be paid through DRC-03 with interest, and missed credit is lost. The finished working papers also support GSTR-9, GSTR-9C where it applies, and any later notice.
points: 30 November deadlines for ITC, amendments and credit notes
Working papers for GSTR-9, 9C and notices
exp: Most painful annual returns are painful because the reconciliation started in December.
